1. **PR description vs. diff mismatch (blocking)** — The title, description, "Root Cause"/"Solution" sections, and claimed test/doc changes all describe an unrelated fix (`mkShellArgs.packages` being dropped in `devshell.nix`, plus a `test/simple/flake.nix` test and `doc/devshell.md` update). The actual diff only adds `default = lib.id;` to the `custom` option in `nix/modules/project/settings/all.nix` — none of the described files, tests, or rationale are present. This can't be reviewed or merged as-is: either the wrong diff was attached to this PR, or two unrelated fixes got merged into one description. Require the author to resubmit so the description, linked issues, and diff actually correspond to the same change (split into two PRs if both fixes are real).

2. **No regression test for the actual change** — Nothing in the diff reproduces or verifies the "`custom` expected to be unique" module-merge error this is supposedly fixing. Add a test (e.g. a project module that ends up with two merged definitions/overlays touching the same package's `custom` setting) that fails on `main` and passes with this change, so the fix is actually demonstrated rather than asserted by comment.

3. **Root cause not shown to be fully addressed** — `default = lib.id;` on an `mkOption` only kicks in when *zero* definitions are supplied for `custom`; it does nothing to resolve a genuine multi-definition conflict (e.g. if some internal code path still sets `custom = lib.mkDefault lib.id;` in more than one merged module for the same package, which is the classic source of this exact nixpkgs error). The PR doesn't explain or show removal of whatever previously produced the "unique" error, so it's unclear whether this one-line change actually fixes the reported bug or just happens to suppress a different, simpler case (option never set at all).

4. **Option description not updated** — The `custom` option's `description` ("A custom function to apply on the Haskell package.") isn't updated to mention it now defaults to the identity function; this affects generated docs/options reference and leaves the default behavior undocumented for users relying on `lib.recursiveUpdate`/composition patterns with `custom`.

5. **Comment doesn't explain the mechanism** — `# Identity function allows composition without conflicts` states the fix's intent but not *why* identity resolves the specific "expected to be unique" merge error; a future maintainer reading this line alone can't tell what regression it guards against. Replace with a comment referencing the actual failure mode (or the issue/discussion number) being fixed.
